newsitem.title: UK: INSTANT VIEW -- UK June retail sales.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW -- UK June retail sales.

text.p: Following is a selection of analysts' comments on data showing UK June retail sales rose 0.6 percent month-on-month and 5.4 percent year-on-year:
"The year on year rate is much higher than expected, which obviously means there have been lots of back revisions to the data. Clearly the trend is very strong."
"It certainly looks as though the Halifax money has given a tremendous boost to the household goods sector -- another sign that consumers have got lots of money and are spending some of it."

"It does confirm the strong underlying trend. Indeed with these back revisions, it suggests the underlying trend is even stronger than we initially thought. The other key message to draw from these figures is that these windfall payments look as though they are going right into the consumer goods sector, particularly the household goods sector. They are not being saved to the extent that was previously thought. This must be something of a worry to the authorities."

"UK retail sales were at the upper end of expectations and should be seen as increasing the risk of another Bank of England rate hike next month. In addition to a strong bottom line, the breakdown of the data is surprisingly robust in key areas and consistent with the upswing in the housing market feeding through into high street spending. Surge in household goods truly remarkable and supported by clothing and footwear. This will certainly worry the Bank of England. May be that the rise in sterling -- which should now see DM 3.10 -- will be enough to stop rates from going up again in August, but a very close call."

"This will reinforce the market's fears that the windfall payments are providing a significant boost to consumer spending. The household goods rise in June was spectacular-- a rise of 21 percent on the year speaks for itself. The worry will be now that July will be just as strong."
